identity.name: Anomalous Privileged Role / Consent Grant Deviating from Admin Learned Baseline — Cortex Identity ABIOC (T1098 / T1484)
identity.summary: A directory-sync / identity-automation account whose learned Cortex baseline is read-and-sync suddenly assigns a privileged directory role and grants a high-risk OAuth consent — Storm-0501 hybrid-cloud identity abuse. The deviation from the account's learned governance baseline plus the causality chain is what the auto-tuned ABIOC fires on.
identity.description: Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) is a first-party Cortex detection type distinct from a hand-authored BIOC: PANW authors and continually tunes ABIOCs against the user, endpoint, and network behavioral profiles Cortex learns per environment, firing on a single suspicious event that carries an identified chain of causality. This scenario exercises that detector class on the IDENTITY plane. It models Storm-0501, the Microsoft-tracked actor that pivots from on-prem compromise into a victim's Entra ID tenant by abusing a compromised Directory Synchronization / identity-automation account: rather than dropping malware, the operator assigns itself (or a controlled principal) a privileged directory role and grants a high-risk OAuth application consent to persist and escalate in the cloud. Cortex has learned that the sync/automation identity is a low-noise governance principal — it reconciles attribute writes and reads directory objects, never assigns Global Administrator, and never consents to Directory.ReadWrite.All-class application scopes. The scenario injects two behavioral deviations from that learned baseline: (a) a privileged directory-role assignment (Global Administrator / Privileged Role Administrator) initiated by the non-governance identity, and (b) a high-risk OAuth consent / service-principal credential grant carrying tenant-wide application scopes. A hand-authored BIOC keyed on a specific bad principal or role id would miss this — every action uses legitimate Entra ID administrative APIs — which is exactly the point: the auto-tuned ABIOC fires on the deviation from the account's learned governance behavior and anchors it to the causality chain (compromised sync account -> privileged role assignment -> tenant-wide consent grant). Two ABIOCs cover the two deviation shapes; supporting validation XQL confirms the account's learned baseline and surfaces the out-of-workflow role assignment; a correlation rule stitches the two ABIOCs into a single rogue-privilege-escalation incident the DC presents as proof that Cortex's behavioral analytics caught novel hybrid-cloud identity abuse no static rule was written for.

campaigns: Hybrid-cloud ransomware and extortion pivoting from on-prem AD into Entra ID via compromised sync/service accounts (2024-2026)

data_sources: Active Directory: Active Directory Object Modification

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-ITDR-010 — Anomalous privileged role/consent grant deviating from the admin learned baseline for Cortex identity ABIOC validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM ingesting Entra ID (Azure AD) audit logs into the msft_azure_ad_signin dataset so directory role-assignment and consent events reach analytics.
A baseline window has elapsed during which the sync/automation identity performed only its read-and-sync activity so Cortex learned the governance-identity profile.

payload.code:
# No known-bad payloads. Emit markers standing in for a directory role
# assignment and a high-risk OAuth consent initiated by a sync/automation
# identity whose learned Cortex baseline never performs either action.
set -euo pipefail
id
echo '[CortexSim] privileged directory-role assignment by non-governance identity'
echo '[CortexSim] high-risk OAuth consent / service-principal credential grant'
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-ITDR-010 rogue privilege escalation emitted'

input_variables.name: SYNC_IDENTITY
input_variables.description: The learned sync/automation identity whose governance baseline the injected role/consent grants deviate from.

expected_artifacts.description: A privileged directory-role assignment (Global Administrator / Privileged Role Administrator) initiated by an identity whose learned baseline never assigns privileged roles.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: category = "RoleManagement" and target_role in (Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator)

expected_artifacts.description: A high-risk OAuth consent or service-principal credential grant carrying tenant-wide application scopes initiated by the non-governance identity.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: activity_display_name in (Consent to application, Add service principal credentials) and oauth_scope contains "Directory.ReadWrite.All"

abiocs.name: ITDR-010 Anomalous Privileged Directory Role Assignment by Non-Governance Identity
abiocs.description: A directory-sync / identity-automation account whose learned Cortex behavioral profile is read-and-sync governance suddenly assigns a privileged directory role (Global Administrator / Privileged Role Administrator). ABIOC anchors the deviation to the causality chain (compromised sync account -> privileged role assignment) rather than to any known-bad principal or role id, catching hybrid-cloud identity abuse that a static rule keyed on a specific bad actor would miss.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin
| filter category = "RoleManagement" and activity_display_name in ("Add member to role", "Add eligible member to role", "Add member to role in PIM requested (permanent)")
| filter initiating_user_principal_name in ("svc-backup@cortexsim-canary.invalid", "sync_svc@cortexsim-canary.invalid", "adconnect@cortexsim-canary.invalid")
| filter target_role in ("Global Administrator", "Privileged Role Administrator", "Application Administrator")
| comp count() as privileged_grants by initiating_user_principal_name, target_role
| filter privileged_grants >= 1
| sort desc privileged_grants
| fields initiating_user_principal_name, target_role, privileged_grants
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned governance-identity baseline (read-and-sync directory activity, no privileged role assignments) -> compromised sync/automation account -> privileged directory-role assignment that diverges from the baseline, anchored to the initiating identity.

abiocs.name: ITDR-010 High-Risk OAuth Consent and App Credential Grant Deviating from Baseline
abiocs.description: A sync/automation identity whose learned baseline never consents to tenant-wide application scopes grants a high-risk OAuth consent or adds service-principal credentials carrying Directory.ReadWrite.All-class scopes. Every action uses legitimate Entra ID application APIs; the ABIOC fires on the deviation from the account's learned consent behavior, anchored to the privileged-role grant that preceded it in the same identity causality chain.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin
| filter category in ("ApplicationManagement", "UserManagement") and activity_display_name in ("Consent to application", "Add app role assignment grant to user", "Add service principal credentials", "Update application - Certificates and secrets management")
| filter initiating_user_principal_name in ("svc-backup@cortexsim-canary.invalid", "sync_svc@cortexsim-canary.invalid", "adconnect@cortexsim-canary.invalid")
| filter oauth_scope contains "Directory.ReadWrite.All" or oauth_scope contains "RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory" or oauth_scope contains "full_access_as_app"
| comp count() as risky_grants by initiating_user_principal_name, oauth_scope
| filter risky_grants >= 1
| sort desc risky_grants
| fields initiating_user_principal_name, oauth_scope, risky_grants
abiocs.causality_anchor: Privileged directory-role assignment by the sync/automation identity -> high-risk OAuth consent / service-principal credential grant carrying tenant-wide scopes that exceeds the account's learned consent baseline, anchored to the preceding role grant.

xql_queries.name: ITDR-010 Privileged Role Assignment Surfaced Outside Governance Workflow
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter category = "RoleManagement" and activity_display_name contains "Add member to role"
| filter target_role in ("Global Administrator", "Privileged Role Administrator")
| comp count() as grants, values(target_role) as roles, earliest(_time) as first_seen by initiating_user_principal_name
| filter grants >= 1
| fields initiating_user_principal_name, roles, grants, first_seen

xql_queries.name: ITDR-010 Sync Account Governance Baseline Learned
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter initiating_user_principal_name = "svc-backup@cortexsim-canary.invalid"
| comp count_distinct(activity_display_name) as baseline_activities by initiating_user_principal_name
| filter baseline_activities >= 1
| fields initiating_user_principal_name, baseline_activities

correlation_rules.name: Rogue Privilege Escalation on Sync Account — ABIOC Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(ITDR-010 Anomalous Privileged Directory Role Assignment by Non-Governance Identity) AND ABIOC(ITDR-010 High-Risk OAuth Consent and App Credential Grant Deviating from Baseline) — fuses the two auto-tuned behavioral deviations on the same tenant+identity into a single rogue-privilege-escalation incident anchored to the sync/automation-account causality chain.

analytics_modules: Cortex XSIAM Analytics — auto-tuned behavioral profiling of per-identity directory-administration and consent activity

products.evidence_query: Two ABIOCs fire on the sync-account governance-baseline deviation; CR-ITDR-0010 stitches them into one rogue-privilege-escalation incident anchored to the identity causality chain.
dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin | filter category = "RoleManagement" | filter initiating_user_principal_name = "svc-backup@cortexsim-canary.invalid"

use_cases.name: Rogue Privileged Role / Consent Grant Detection via Cortex ABIOC
use_cases.description: Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs learn a directory-sync / identity-automation account's read-and-sync governance baseline and detect anomalous privileged role assignments and high-risk OAuth consent grants by that account, anchored to its causality chain, where no static rule was written for the legitimate Entra ID APIs involved.

test_cases.objective: Cortex learns the sync-account governance baseline and an injected role/consent deviation fires both ABIOCs.
preconditions: XSIAM ingesting Entra ID audit logs into msft_azure_ad_signin.
Baseline window elapsed with the sync account performing only read-and-sync activity.
steps: Let the governance baseline window elapse.
Assign a privileged directory role and grant a high-risk OAuth consent from the sync identity.
Observe both ABIOCs fire and CR-ITDR-0010 raise a rogue-privilege-escalation incident.
success_criteria: ABIOC `ITDR-010 Anomalous Privileged Directory Role Assignment by Non-Governance Identity` fires.
ABIOC `ITDR-010 High-Risk OAuth Consent and App Credential Grant Deviating from Baseline` fires.
Correlation CR-ITDR-0010 raises one stitched rogue-privilege-escalation incident.

preventive_controls: Remove standing directory-administration privileges from sync/automation accounts; use least-privilege application permissions and PIM just-in-time elevation with approval for any privileged role.
Restrict user and admin OAuth consent to an allowlist of vetted applications and block tenant-wide consent to Directory.ReadWrite.All-class scopes.
Alert on any privileged directory-role assignment or high-risk consent initiated by an account whose baseline is non-interactive read-and-sync.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-identity directory-administration and consent baseline rather than hand-authoring static rules for individual roles or app ids.
Alert on a sync/automation identity assigning a privileged directory role.
Alert on a consent or service-principal credential grant that exceeds an identity's learned consent behavior.
